Synchronise retained bins across samples

Source: R/g1_windows.R
synchronize_bins.Rd

Apply a shared bin filter to several samples: for each sample the removed bins are the bins of gr_cn_list[[s]] with no exactly matching bin (same seqnames, start, end, strand) in gr_filtered_list[[s]]; the removed bins of the samples in union_samples are pooled (unique coordinates), and every sample's retained bins that exactly match a pooled removed bin are dropped. A bin is therefore kept only if it survived filtering in all union_samples (among the bins present in each sample's unfiltered set).

Usage

synchronize_bins(
  gr_cn_list,
  gr_filtered_list,
  union_samples = names(gr_cn_list)
)

Arguments

gr_cn_list

Named list (or GRangesList) of the unfiltered per-sample bins.

gr_filtered_list

Named list (or GRangesList) of the per-sample retained bins (gr_filtered.rds, e.g. unlisted filter_windows() output), with the same names as gr_cn_list.

union_samples

Names of the samples whose removed bins are pooled. Default: all samples.

Value

A list with

filtered

named list of GRanges: gr_filtered_list with the pooled removed bins dropped; metadata columns are kept.

removed

named list of GRanges: per-sample removed bins.

removed_union

GRanges of pooled removed bins (no metadata columns).

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(seq(1, by = 10, length.out = 6),
                                                      width = 10))
res <- synchronize_bins(
  list(a = gr, b = gr),
  list(a = gr[-2], b = gr[-5])
)
res$filtered$a   # bins 2 and 5 removed in both samples
#> GRanges object with 4 ranges and 0 metadata columns:
#>       seqnames    ranges strand
#>          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle>
#>   [1]     chr1      1-10      *
#>   [2]     chr1     21-30      *
#>   [3]     chr1     31-40      *
#>   [4]     chr1     51-60      *
#>   -------
#>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths
